planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost; Bala is a key Ayurvedic Dashamoola herb grown as a warm-season annual outside the tropics.

directions: Direct sow into average, well-drained soil in full sun; Bala is a shrubby perennial herb reaching 2-4 feet, with heart-shaped, velvety leaves and small yellow flowers. It is a key member of the Ayurvedic Dashamoola (ten roots) formula group, traditionally used in respiratory and nervous-system tonics. It is a warm-season plant with only half-hardy frost tolerance, best grown as an annual in temperate climates and as a true perennial in zones 9-11.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Parijat's fragrant flowers open at dusk and drop by dawn, earning it the name 'tree of sorrow.'

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in well-drained soil; Parijat is a small deciduous tree or large shrub bearing intensely fragrant white flowers with orange centers that open only at dusk and drop by dawn each morning, a dramatic nightly display that gave it the common name 'tree of sorrow.' In Ayurveda, the flowers and leaves are used for fever and arthritis, and the orange corolla tubes yield a traditional dye. It is tender below roughly zone 9 and best grown as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside true tropical and subtropical climates.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost into well-drained soil in full sun; Kantakari is a spiny, sprawling nightshade relative, handle with care when working around it.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun; Kantakari is a spiny, trailing nightshade relative bearing purple-blue flowers followed by yellow berries, a classic Dashamoola herb in Ayurveda used traditionally for cough and asthma. It is an annual or short-lived perennial in warm climates, thriving in full sun with only moderate water needs. Handle it with gloves when weeding or harvesting, since the stems and leaves carry sharp spines typical of this genus.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into moist, well-drained soil in full sun; Arjuna is a riverine tree that tolerates seasonal flooding, a good companion to the already-present Terminalia chebula and bellirica.

directions: Plant in full sun in moist, well-drained soil; Arjuna is a large, fast-growing deciduous riverine tree whose bark decoction is one of the major Ayurvedic cardiotonic (heart-support) preparations, rounding out the already-present chebula and bellirica myrobalans into a more complete Terminalia medicinal grouping. It tolerates seasonal flooding in its native riparian habitat, unlike most of its genus relatives, and makes a substantial shade tree given room to mature. It has no frost tolerance and is suited only to true tropical and subtropical zones 10-12.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost into average, well-drained soil in full sun; Thumbai is an easy, low-maintenance herb that tolerates poor soil well.

directions: Direct sow into average, well-drained soil in full sun; Thumbai is a low-growing, easy-to-grow mint-family annual or short-lived perennial bearing whorled clusters of small white flowers, used across South India for fever, colds, insect bites, and various skin conditions. It tolerates poor soil well and is treated as a common roadside herb in its native range, making it a low-maintenance addition to an Ayurvedic or ethnobotanical herb garden. Grow it as a warm-season annual outside zones 9-11.

planting.note: Direct sow in cool weather into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Chukka Kura bolts quickly in heat, so plan for a cool-season harvest window.

directions: Direct sow into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Chukka Kura is a fast-growing, tender annual leafy green with broad, tart, sour leaves similar in use to spinach, ready for first harvest in just 30-40 days. It is a staple souring agent in Andhra cuisine, used in dal and chutney preparations. It prefers cool-season growth and bolts quickly in summer heat, so succession-sow in cooler weather for a continuous supply, a crop well suited to Gulf Coast winter gardening.

planting.note: Plant root tubers in spring into well-drained, sandy loam in part shade to full sun; Safed Musli is grown from tubers or root cuttings far more often than true seed.

directions: Plant root tubers into well-drained, sandy loam in part shade to full sun; Safed Musli is a tuberous-rooted perennial herb, a relative of the common spider plant, grown specifically for its fasciculated root tubers, which are a prized Ayurvedic rasayana (rejuvenating adaptogen) and traditional aphrodisiac. It is propagated almost entirely from tuber divisions or root cuttings rather than true seed, and needs a tropical or warm subtropical climate with no frost tolerance. Harvest roots after the foliage dies back, typically 6-12 months after planting.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Sonapatha grows fast but needs a long warm season, with flowers opening only at night.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil; Sonapatha is a fast-growing deciduous tree with huge pinnate leaves and dramatic purple-red flower spikes that open only at night, maturing into giant sword-like seed pods that give the tree its common names (broken bones tree, Indian trumpet flower). Bark and root are used in the Ayurvedic Dashamoola formula, while young pods and flowers are eaten as a vegetable in northeastern India and Southeast Asia. It has no frost tolerance and needs true tropical or subtropical conditions, zones 10-12.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil has warmed following last frost into well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Shalaparni is a nitrogen-fixing legume, benefiting neighboring plantings.

directions: Direct sow into well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Shalaparni is a small perennial legume subshrub with trifoliate leaves, part of the Ayurvedic Dashamoola (ten roots) group used for respiratory and digestive tonics. Like other legumes it fixes its own nitrogen, benefiting the soil and neighboring plants in a mixed herb bed. It grows easily in warm climates or as a container plant brought indoors for winter outside zones 9-11.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Kutaj's seeds are traditionally sold in Indian markets as Indrajav or Indrajao.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in well-drained soil; Kutaj is a small deciduous tree whose bark decoction is a classic Ayurvedic remedy for dysentery, with its seeds traditionally sold in Indian markets under the name Indrajav or Indrajao. It is slow to establish from seed but grows into a modest flowering tree over a few years, bearing fragrant white flowers. It has no frost tolerance and requires a true tropical or subtropical climate, zones 10-12.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade; Kali Musli is a rhizomatous herb grown for its root much like Safed Musli, but a different genus.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions into humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade; Kali Musli is a rhizomatous herb with grass-like leaves, grown for its dark-skinned rhizomatous roots, which are a traditional Ayurvedic aphrodisiac and general tonic distinct from the pale-rooted Safed Musli despite the similar common name and use. It spreads gradually by rhizome in a shaded woodland-edge or herb-garden setting. It has no frost tolerance and needs a warm, humid climate to thrive, zones 9-11.
